steps.explain: Find stationary points
steps.work: \text{Set the derivative to zero:}\\ 10\pi r - \pi r^2 = 0\\ \pi r(10 - r) = 0\\ \text{Since a cone must have a positive radius } (r > 0)\text{, we divide by } \pi r \text{ to get:}\\ 10 - r = 0 \implies r = 10

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the function:
\( f(x) = x^8 \)
questions.hint: Use the integration power rule: increase the power by 1 and divide by the new power.

steps.explain: Understand 'primitive'
steps.work: \text{The primitive of a function is its antiderivative (or indefinite integral).}

steps.explain: Apply the power rule for integration
steps.work: \text{To integrate } x^n \text{, we increase the power by 1 and divide by the new power:}\\ \int x^8 \, dx = \frac{x^{8+1}}{8+1} = \frac{x^9}{9}

steps.explain: Add the constant of integration
steps.work: \text{Since it is an indefinite integral, we must add the arbitrary constant } C:\\ \frac{x^9}{9} + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the function:
\( f(x) = 4x \)
questions.hint: Integrate x to x^2 / 2, keeping the coefficient.

steps.explain: Understand 'primitive'
steps.work: \text{The primitive is the antiderivative, or indefinite integral, of the function.}

steps.explain: Apply the power rule
steps.work: \text{For a term } kx^n \text{, the integral is } k\left(\frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\right).\text{ Here } n=1 \text{, so we increase the power to 2 and divide by 2:}\\ \int 4x \, dx = 4\left(\frac{x^2}{2}\right)

steps.explain: Simplify and add constant
steps.work: \text{Simplify the coefficient and add the constant of integration } C:\\ 2x^2 + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the constant function:
\( f(x) = 6 \)
questions.hint: The primitive of a constant k is kx + C.

steps.explain: Understand the integral of a constant
steps.work: \text{A constant } k \text{ can be thought of as } kx^0\text{. Integrating it yields } \frac{kx^1}{1} = kx.

steps.explain: Integrate
Add constant of integration
steps.work: \text{Always add } C \text{ for indefinite integrals:}\\ 6x + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the function:
\( f(x) = 15x^4 \)
questions.hint: Add 1 to power of 4, then divide coefficient 15 by 5.

steps.explain: Apply the power rule
steps.work: \text{Increase the power of } x \text{ from 4 to 5, then divide the term by the new power 5:}\\ \int 15x^4 \, dx = 15\left(\frac{x^5}{5}\right)

steps.explain: Simplify and add constant
steps.work: \text{Simplify the coefficient and add } C:\\ 3x^5 + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the function:
\( f(x) = 6x + 6x^2 - 4x^3 \)
questions.hint: Integrate each polynomial term individually.

steps.explain: Integrate term by term
steps.work: \text{Apply the power rule to each term individually. Increase each power by 1 and divide by the new power.}

steps.explain: First term
Second term
Third term
Combine and add constant

questions.stem:
Find the primitive after expanding brackets first:
\( f(x) = 2x(x - 3) \)
questions.hint: Expand brackets to 2x^2 - 6x, then integrate.

steps.explain: Expand the brackets
steps.work: \text{Before integrating, expand the expression } 2x(x - 3) \text{ by distributing } 2x:\\ 2x^2 - 6x

steps.explain: Integrate term by term
steps.work: \text{Apply the power rule to each term.}\\ \text{For } 2x^2 \text{, the integral is } \frac{2x^3}{3}.\\ \text{For } -6x \text{, the integral is } -\frac{6x^2}{2} = -3x^2.

steps.explain: Add the constant of integration
steps.work: \text{Since this is an indefinite integral, add } + C \text{ at the end:}\\ \frac{2x^3}{3} - 3x^2 + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive after expanding brackets first:
\( f(x) = (x + 2)(x - 4) \)
questions.hint: Expand using FOIL to get x^2 - 2x - 8, then integrate.

steps.explain: Expand the brackets
steps.work: \text{Use the FOIL method to expand } (x + 2)(x - 4):\\ x^2 - 4x + 2x - 8 = x^2 - 2x - 8

steps.explain: Integrate term by term
steps.work: \text{Apply the power rule.}\\ \text{The integral of } x^2 \text{ is } \frac{x^3}{3}.\\ \text{The integral of } -2x \text{ is } -x^2.\\ \text{The integral of } -8 \text{ is } -8x.

steps.explain: Add the constant of integration
steps.work: \text{Always add } + C \text{ for indefinite integrals:}\\ \frac{x^3}{3} - x^2 - 8x + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive after expanding brackets first:
\( f(x) = (3x - 2)^2 \)
questions.hint: Expand the perfect square trinomial to 9x^2 - 12x + 4, then integrate.

steps.explain: Expand the perfect square
steps.work: \text{Use the formula } (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2 \text{ to expand } (3x - 2)^2:\\ (3x)^2 - 2(3x)(2) + 2^2 = 9x^2 - 12x + 4

steps.explain: Integrate term by term
steps.work: \text{Apply the power rule.}\\ \int 9x^2 \, dx = 9\left(\frac{x^3}{3}\right) = 3x^3\\ \int -12x \, dx = -12\left(\frac{x^2}{2}\right) = -6x^2\\ \int 4 \, dx = 4x

steps.explain: Combine and add constant

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the function:
\( f(x) = (x+3)^4 \)
questions.hint: Apply composite linear integration rule with a = 1.

steps.explain: Use the composite integration rule
steps.work: \text{For a linear function to a power } (ax+b)^n \text{, the integral is } \frac{(ax+b)^{n+1}}{a(n+1)}.

steps.explain: Apply the rule to the function
steps.work: \text{Here } a = 1\text{, } b = 3\text{, and } n = 4\text{. Increase the power from 4 to 5, and divide by } 5 \times 1 = 5.\\ \int (x+3)^4 \, dx = \frac{(x+3)^5}{5}

steps.explain: Add the constant of integration
steps.work: \text{Always add } + C \text{ for indefinite integrals:}\\ \frac{(x+3)^5}{5} + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the function:
\( f(x) = (x-2)^6 \)
questions.hint: Apply composite linear integration rule.

steps.explain: Integrate composite function
steps.work: \text{Apply the composite linear integration rule. Increase the power from 6 to 7, and divide by 7(1).}\\ \int (x-2)^6 \, dx = \frac{(x-2)^7}{7} + C

questions.stem:
Find the primitive of the function:
\( f(x) = (3x-1)^4 \)
questions.hint: The coefficient of x is a = 3. Divide by 3 * 5 = 15.

steps.explain: Apply composite linear integration rule
steps.work: \text{The coefficient of } x \text{ is } a = 3\text{. Increase power to 5, and divide by } a \times n = 3 \times 5 = 15.\\ \int (3x-1)^4 \, dx = \frac{(3x-1)^5}{3 \times 5} + C

steps.explain: Simplify denominator

questions.stem:
Find the primitive after writing as a power of \( x \):
\( f(x) = \frac{1}{x^3} \)
questions.hint: Rewrite as x^(-3) first, then integrate.

steps.explain: Rewrite in index form
steps.work: \text{Before integrating, move } x^3 \text{ to the numerator using a negative index:}\\ f(x) = x^{-3}

steps.explain: Integrate using power rule
steps.work: \text{Increase the power by 1 (-3 + 1 = -2), and divide by the new power -2:}\\ \int x^{-3} \, dx = \frac{x^{-2}}{-2} + C

steps.explain: Convert back to positive index

questions.stem:
Find the primitive after writing as a power of \( x \):
\( f(x) = \sqrt[3]{x} \)
questions.hint: Rewrite in rational exponent index form x^(1/3).

steps.explain: Rewrite in index form
steps.work: \text{Convert the cube root into a fractional exponent:}\\ f(x) = x^{\frac{1}{3}}

steps.explain: Integrate using power rule
steps.work: \text{Increase the power by 1: } \frac{1}{3} + 1 = \frac{4}{3}\text{. Divide by } \frac{4}{3} \text{, which is equivalent to multiplying by } \frac{3}{4}:\\ \int x^{\frac{1}{3}} \, dx = \frac{x^{\frac{4}{3}}}{\frac{4}{3}} + C = \frac{3}{4}x^{\frac{4}{3}} + C

questions.stem:
Find the equation of the curve passing through the point \( (2, 4) \) with gradient function:
\( f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x + 2 \)
questions.hint: Integrate gradient function to get family y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x + C, then plug in (2, 4).

steps.explain: Integrate the derivative to find the curve family
steps.work: \text{The equation of the curve } y \text{ is the integral of the gradient function } f'(x):\\ y = \int (3x^2 - 6x + 2) \, dx = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x + C

steps.explain: Substitute coordinates to solve for C
steps.work: \text{Since the curve passes through } (2, 4)\text{, substitute } x = 2 \text{ and } y = 4:\\ 4 = (2)^3 - 3(2)^2 + 2(2) + C\\ 4 = 8 - 12 + 4 + C \implies 4 = C

steps.explain: State final curve equation
steps.work: \text{Substitute } C = 4 \text{ back into the original equation:}\\ y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x + 4

questions.stem: If \( f'(x) = 6x - 2 \) and \( f(2) = 11 \), find the value of \( f(3) \).
questions.hint: Integrate f'(x) to find f(x), solve for C with f(2) = 11, then calculate f(3).

steps.explain: Integrate derivative to get function f(x)
steps.work: \text{Find the primitive of } f'(x):\\ f(x) = \int (6x - 2) \, dx = 3x^2 - 2x + C

steps.explain: Substitute x = 2 and f(2) = 11 to solve for C
steps.work: \text{We are given } f(2) = 11:\\ 11 = 3(2)^2 - 2(2) + C\\ 11 = 12 - 4 + C \implies 11 = 8 + C \implies C = 3

steps.explain: State complete function f(x)
Evaluate f(3)
steps.work: \text{Substitute } x = 3 \text{ into the complete function:}\\ f(3) = 3(3)^2 - 2(3) + 3 = 27 - 6 + 3 = 24

questions.stem: The graph of y = x³ + x² − x + 2 is sketched below. The points A and B are the turning points.

parts.stem: Find the coordinates of A and B.
parts.hint: Differentiate and set the gradient equal to zero. Factor the quadratic to find both x-coordinates, then substitute each into the original curve.

steps.explain: Differentiate the cubic to get the gradient.

parts.stem: For what values of x is the curve concave up? Give reasons for your answer.
parts.hint: Concavity is determined by the second derivative. Find where it is positive.

steps.explain: Differentiate again to obtain the second derivative.

steps.explain: Concave up means the second derivative is positive. Solve the inequality.
So the curve is concave up to the right of x=−1/3.

parts.stem: For what values of k does the equation x³ + x² − x + 2 = k have three real solutions?
parts.hint: Think of y=k as a horizontal line. It cuts the cubic three times only when its height is strictly between the local minimum and local maximum.

steps.explain: The graph has a local maximum of 3 at A and a local minimum of 49/27 at B.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="50%" height="auto" viewBox="0 0 440 280"><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white"/><path d="M35 235H405M220 255V20" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M45 220 C86 200 105 76 150 56 C181 44 207 102 232 147 C255 190 276 202 300 184 C333 158 354 70 400 42" fill="none" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="150" cy="56" r="5" fill="#ef4444"/><circle cx="232" cy="147" r="5" fill="#8b5cf6"/><path d="M150 235V56M232 235V147" stroke="#f59e0b" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><text x="150" y="255" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial" font-size="12">A(−1,3)</text><text x="250" y="163" font-family="Arial" font-size="12">B(1/3,49/27)</text><text x="407" y="233" font-family="Arial" font-size="14">x</text><text x="226" y="20" font-family="Arial" font-size="14">y</text></svg>

steps.explain: A horizontal line between those two heights crosses the cubic once on each of its three branches. At either turning-point height, two intersections merge, so there are not three distinct solutions.
Therefore k must lie strictly between the turning-point y-values.
